title: Superfluid helium
abstract: We are interested in modelling superfluid helium-4, the common isotope of helium, of atomic number 4. We present a mathematically solvable toy model of the phase transition between the normal liquid and superfluid phases and use it to show how an order parameter might be obtained for the superfluid.
summary: This theoretical paper models the liquid-superfluid phase transition in helium using an abstract toy model based on dense random graphs. By employing the mathematical formalism of graphons in the infinite system limit, the authors demonstrate how a difference in symmetry can naturally define an order parameter distinguishing the two distinct phases.
main_problem: The primary goal is modeling the phase transition between normal liquid ($	ext{He I}$) and superfluid ($	ext{He II}$) helium-4, focusing on developing a theoretical framework to identify an order parameter.
main_result: The authors propose using graph theory in the infinite system limit to show how symmetry differences can define an order parameter distinguishing the two distinct phases.
method: The analysis relies heavily on constructing and analyzing 'toy models' based on dense random graphs, utilizing the mathematical formalism of graphons derived from Lovász et al. [42].
model_or_system: The system is superfluid helium-4 ($	ext{He}$), modeled abstractly using an edge/triangle graph model defined on $n$ vertices. The analysis maps this to constraints on edge density ($\epsilon$) and triangle density ($	au$).
key_observables: Order parameter, entropy (in the infinite system limit), thermal conductivity, and viscosity.
important_parameters: Edge density ($\epsilon$), triangle density ($	au$), and the transition point between $	ext{He I}$ and $	ext{He II}$.
main_assumptions: The model is a 'toy model' whose formalism (infinite system limits) is not guaranteed to apply to all physical transitions, especially the fluid/solid one.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate simplified P-T phase diagrams for ${}^4	ext{He}$ and $	ext{CO}_2$, and later show the structure of possible phases in the edge/triangle model (e.g., regions A(2,0), B(1,1), F(1,1)) represented by graphons.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical problem ($	ext{He I}/	ext{He II}$ transition) to introducing a mathematical analogy using random graphs and their infinite limits (graphons). It then uses this framework to derive structural differences that serve as order parameters for the superfluid phase.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the use of advanced tools like graphons and infinite system limits to define symmetry-breaking order parameters is mathematically sophisticated and relevant to understanding emergent order in complex many-body systems.
